# What `granule guest verify` asserts about the guest the "build" chapter
# builds: boot it, run each of these in it as root, print a verdict. No
# commit, no tag, no image -- verify judges, it does not produce.
#
# The format is a [name] line and then the shell that tests it. The name
# is the sentence the verdict is reported as, so it is written as the
# claim rather than as the command.

[the machine the Dockerfile described actually booted]
test -f /etc/os-release
grep -q 'ID=debian' /etc/os-release

[nginx is installed and enabled, not merely present in the image]
command -v nginx
systemctl is-enabled nginx

[nginx started on its own at boot and answers on the port the image EXPOSEs]
systemctl is-active nginx
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/whoami | grep -q 'granule demo guest'

[the guest half granule packed is the one that is running]
test -f /etc/granule/guest-contract
command -v granule-agent

[the disk grew onto the space it was given]
df -h / | tail -1
